title: Planckian dissipation: definitions and inference
summary: A linear resistivity does not by itself measure a Planckian lifetime. Specify the relaxation channel, residual rate, frequency convention and transport model.

claims.statement: “Planckian” commonly describes a specified relaxation rate on the scale $k_BT/\hbar$, with a dimensionless coefficient of order unity. It is not a theorem inferred from a resistivity curve that happens to be linear in temperature. Transport, optical, single-particle, thermalization and quantum-chaos times probe different correlation functions and need not be equal.
claims.conditions: A lifetime must specify transport/optical/single-particle/thermal/chaos channel, residual term and h-versus-hbar convention. Single-band Drude extraction assumes appropriate n and m*.
claims.verificationScope: See each source verification label; this ledger does not certify primary findings.

claims.statement: The resistivity slope alone does not supply the carrier density $n$ or transport mass $m^\ast$. Multiband conduction, changing spectral weight, angular scattering and vertex effects can invalidate this simple inversion. Sheet resistance and bulk resistivity must also use consistent thickness conventions.

claims.statement: Use a Planckian-scale observation to formulate a falsifiable normal-state model. Ask which spectral weight, carrier estimate and scattering anisotropy would support or reject the proposed interpretation. Proximity to superconductivity can motivate a mechanism study, but it does not establish that faster scattering raises the critical temperature.
